area: Store departments / sections / zones and how staff bind to parts of a store (Team Leader design input)
findings:
SUMMARY: Big Ambitions has NO department/section/zone/aisle concept anywhere. The finest native units are: BusinessType (a whole store type) -> a flat BusinessProduct[] product list -> individual ItemInstance shelves/registers. Staff bind to a store ONLY through schedule WorkShift entries, each pointing at one assignable ItemInstance id (in practice: cash registers / points of sale, plus cleaning stations) for an hour range on a day. There is NO restock request->approve workflow: restock is player-manual, automatic shelf redistribution from back stock, or a standing weekly DeliveryContract. The "Team Leader owns a department, raises stock requests, Store Manager approves" loop must be 100% mod-invented. Recommendation: model a department as a mod-data named bucket of product itemNames within one supervised store (option a), not game categories (none exist) and not a station subset (stations aren't product-scoped).

=== 1. First-class department/section/zone entity? CONFIRMED NO ===
Searched all ~2278 files for class names matching Zone|Section|Aisle|Department and for the word "aisle". The only "Zone" types are outdoor/unrelated: AiSpawnerZone, BuildingOutsideHangoutZone(Controller/Spawner), Player.Sound/AudioZone, ExitZone/ExitZoneDespawner, CityMapNeighborhoodZones. "Section" only appears as UI.Smartphone.Apps.MyEmployees/MyEmployeeCandidateSection (a list section in the hire UI). Nothing groups shelves, staff, or products into a named sub-area of a single store. This matches the existing mod's DECISIONS.md D7 ("No department concept visible... BusinessType is the finest business-structure unit exposed") - now re-confirmed against Build 3672. SchedulePartitioner has a "SchedulePartition" but that is a transient auto-scheduler fairness grouping (~3 workstations per group for coverage math), rebuilt every schedule pass, never persisted, never player-visible - not a department.

=== 2. How the game groups a store's products ===
- Per-store product set: BusinessType.businessProducts is a flat BusinessProduct[] of { string itemName; float impact }. impact >= 1 => "primary product", impact < 1 => secondary. Helpers on BusinessType: GetPrimaryProducts(), GetAllProducts(), GetPrimaryRetailProducts(), IsPrimaryProduct(itemName), GetProductImpact(itemName). No sub-grouping, no category tree, no "Frozen/Produce" style buckets. A store either sells an item or it doesn't, weighted by impact.
- Item taxonomy is the [Flags] ItemType enum (members enumerated in EnumHelpers.cs ToStringFast): Decoration, RetailProduct, ServiceProduct, PointOfSale, EmployeeWorkstation, StorageShelf, ShowcaseShelf, FactoryMachine, ActivityItem, Security, Seat, Desk, Table, Sink, Toilet, WorkoutMachine, Computer, ... This is a FUNCTIONAL type, not a merchandising category. There is no category field on products.
- Shelves are NOT typed by product category. A ShowcaseShelfController (ItemType.ShowcaseShelf) holds exactly ONE stock item at a time: ItemInstance.GetStockInstance().itemName is the product currently on it (player-assigned or auto-filled). Each shelf ITEM (not instance) has Item.itemsThatCanShowcase (a whitelist of product itemNames it can physically display, e.g. a fridge vs a clothing rack) and Item.defaultShelfItemName - this static whitelist is the closest thing to "shelf typed by product category," but it is item metadata, not an instance grouping. StorageShelfController (ItemType.StorageShelf, tag isstockcontainer) is back-room bulk cargo storage.
- YES, shelves can be enumerated per store with their assigned product. Pattern used by RetailBusinessSimulator.SetUpAvailableShowcaseShelves() and GetRestockableItemsByStockItemName(): iterate buildingRegistration.itemInstances.Values, filter (ItemCached.type & (ItemType.ShowcaseShelf | ItemType.PointOfSale)) != 0, then GetStockInstance().itemName is the product and GetStockInstance().amount / GetStockInstance().GetMaxStockCapacity(itemInstance) is the fill level. They build Dictionary<string productItemName, List<ItemInstance> shelves>. BuildingRegistration.GetItemsOfType(ItemType) is a ready helper. ItemInstance also exposes id, parentId, stackedItems, CanRestockItem(), AddressCached.

=== 3. How a staff member binds to a specific station/shelf/task ===
- The ONLY binding is the schedule. BuildingRegistration.scheduleDays : List<ScheduleDay>; ScheduleDay.workShifts : List<WorkShift>; WorkShift = { int startingHour; int endingHour; string employeeId; string itemInstanceId; WorkShiftType type }. itemInstanceId points at one specific assignable ItemInstance. So an employee is bound to one item instance for a given hour range / day / shift-type. Nothing finer, nothing spatial.
- The live station MonoBehaviour EmployeeStationController.GetEmployeeWorkShift() matches WorkShift.itemInstanceId == this.ItemInstance.id for the current hour to decide who to spawn at the register. Reusable read: EmployeeHelper.GetEmployeeAtStationAndHour(registration, stationId, hour) and IsEmployeeStationEmployedAtHour(...).
- Assignable items = BuildingRegistration.GetAssignableItems(): item.assignable == true AND one of item.suitableSkills is in (BusinessType.employeePrimarySkills UNION BuildingType.requiredBuildingSkills). For a retail store this is essentially the cash registers / points of sale (skill ba:skill_customerservice) plus cleaning stations. SHOWCASE SHELVES ARE GENERALLY NOT ASSIGNABLE - customers self-serve from them; keeping them stocked is a player TodoTask or a delivery contract, not a manned post. So there is no native "employee mans the frozen shelves."
- EmployeeInstance.assignedWorkStationItems : List<string> is a DERIVED cache (UpdateAssignedWorkStationItems()) of the item NAMES (e.g. ba:itemname_cashregister) the employee is scheduled on, including parent and stacked-child item names. Names, not instance ids. Used only to satisfy the WorksOnItem job demand.
- WorksOnItem : JobDemand, IEquipmentDemand, IScheduleDemand, IWorkStationFilter (Entities.Employee.JobDemands.Requirements/WorksOnItem.cs) is the game's "this employee only works these item types" mechanism. itemNames : string[]; AcceptsWorkStation(WorkStationInfo, BuildingRegistration) matches by item NAME (and parent / stacked children), never by a spatial group or a chosen individual instance. Consumed by SchedulePartitioner for auto-scheduling.
- Can the mod tell "employee X works the frozen shelves"? Only transitively and only if the mod itself defines "frozen": enumerate every WorkShift with employeeId == X, resolve itemInstanceId -> ItemInstance. For a register that tells you which STORE, not which products (registers ring up everything). There is no game data linking an employee to a product set or a shelf group.

=== 4. Restock request/approve mechanism? NONE. ===
No request->approve workflow exists. Three restock paths, none with an approval step or an employee actor:
- Player TodoTask flag (informational only): RetailBusinessSimulator.UpdateStockTasksFromFurniture -> ItemHelper.UpdateStockTodoTasks(itemInstance) (ItemHelper.cs ~729) creates TodoTaskType.LowStock when a shelf/POS drops to <= 25% of GetMaxStockCapacity (Priority.Medium) and TodoTaskType.EmptyStock at 0 (Priority.High), keyed by address + stock itemName + item instance id. Auto-completed (BusinessHelper.CompleteStockTask) when stock recovers. This is the closest thing to "someone flags low stock" but the flag lands on the PLAYER's global to-do list; no manager, no approval.
- Automatic internal redistribution: ReStockingHelper.RedistributeStockByPercentage / RefillSingleItemWithLimit move stock the store ALREADY OWNS from back-room containers (tag isstockcontainer) and parked vehicles onto the showcase shelves, proportional to each shelf's missing percentage. Fired hourly at the store's last closing hour via RetailBusinessSimulator.RestockShelvesIfItsTime() / IsRestockTime(). Buys nothing.
- Automatic buying: DeliveryContract (Entities/DeliveryContract.cs), a standing order of DeliveryContractItem { itemName, amount, amountOrderedLastWeek } with wholesaleAddress + businessAddress, repeatingOrder, nextDeliveryDay, deliveryFee, TotalPricePerDelivery. Held in SaveGameManager.Current.DeliveryContracts (flat list; keyed by (store, wholesaler), so a store can have SEVERAL). Player-configured in the store's BizMan Deliveries tab. Edits gated by DeliveryHelper.CanModifyContract(nextDeliveryDay) (Monday lock). Siblings: FurnitureDeliveryContract, FoodDeliveryContract, VehicleDeliveryContract; and the HQ ImportPartnership (importer->warehouse, the ba:skill_purchasingagent HQ plan).
- Manual: player drives to a wholesaler, buys boxes, hauls them, drops on storage shelves.
CONSEQUENCE: the "Team Leader raises a per-department stock request -> Store Manager approves the buy" loop does not exist and cannot be expressed with game entities. The mod already implements the manager half (StoreManager.Interop.DeliveryContracts.PlanAndApply: weekly retune of each contract line toward amountOrderedLastWeek + a capped buffer top-up, then scale-to-fit against StoreAssignment.WeeklyRestockBudgetCap). A "request" is a mod-domain proposal; "approval" is that same weekly pass accepting/trimming it.

=== 5. RECOMMENDATION: model "department" as option (a), leanest form ===
Option (b) "group by game product category" is INFEASIBLE - there are no categories. Option (c) "subset of stations" is INFEASIBLE as a stock model - stations (registers) are not product-scoped. So: option (a), a mod-owned named bucket of product itemNames within one supervised store.

Concrete shape (lives in the same GameInstance.modData blob as StoreManagerPlan):
- Department { string Name; string StoreAddress; List<string> ProductItemNames; string TeamLeaderEmployeeId; per-department budget share / priority }.
- Player fills ProductItemNames by picking from the store's BusinessType.GetAllProducts() (a ModOptions dropdown, or the existing options panel). Default seeding options: one department = all primary products (GetPrimaryProducts()), or auto-split primary products into N even chunks, so a player who doesn't care still gets a working setup.
- "Team Leader handles their section's stock requests": the weekly planner computes a proposed order PER DEPARTMENT - for each ProductItemName, project days-of-stock from real throughput (reuse DeliveryContractItem.amountOrderedLastWeek, already used by DeliveryContracts.ComputeTarget, plus BuildingHelper.CountTotalResourcesInStock) and propose an amount. That proposal IS the request.
- "Store Manager approves the buying": the Store Manager weekly pass sums all department requests for a store, applies the store-level WeeklyRestockBudgetCap, trims (pro-rata, or primary-first, or by a TL priority flag) if over budget, then writes the MERGED result into the store's existing DeliveryContract line amounts (the game has one contract per (store,wholesaler); departments are a bookkeeping layer ABOVE the contract, never separate contracts). The digest/Feedback already in the mod reports per-department spend and lists any trimmed requests as attention items.
- Role wiring: bind Team Leader exactly like the Store Manager is being bound (its own custom skill, its own HQ BizMan tab, scheduled at the HQ). The Team Leader<->department link is Department.TeamLeaderEmployeeId in mod data only. Do NOT try to express it via WorkShift.itemInstanceId - that would need a fake assignable item per department plus Harmony on the scheduler.
Why least-invasive: no new game entity, no Harmony on RetailBusinessSimulator or the scheduler, no fake items placed in the store, reuses BusinessType.businessProducts for the picklist and the single existing DeliveryContract write path. Departments are invisible to the game; they only shape what the mod writes into the contract.

Optional spatial flavor (opt-in, keep fragile part quarantined): also let the player tag specific ShowcaseShelf ItemInstance ids into a department (enumerate via GetItemsOfType(ItemType.ShowcaseShelf) + GetStockInstance().itemName) and derive ProductItemNames from what sits on those shelves. Instance ids churn when items are removed/replaced during a remodel, so make it self-healing: drop unknown ids on load and fall back to the product-name list, which stays the robust core.

feasibility: The DEPARTMENT concept itself: NATIVE / mod-data only - no Harmony, no game patching. Model it as a named bucket of product itemNames per store in GameInstance.modData; drive it into the store's existing DeliveryContract via the mod's current write path (DeliveryHelper.CanModifyContract-gated). Reads needed are all public: BusinessType.GetAllProducts()/GetPrimaryProducts(), BuildingRegistration.GetItemsOfType(ItemType.ShowcaseShelf)/itemInstances, ItemInstance.GetStockInstance(), DeliveryContractItem.amountOrderedLastWeek, BuildingHelper.CountTotalResourcesInStock. The Team Leader ROLE (custom skill + own HQ BizMan tab + wage scale) carries the already-documented Harmony fragility (SkillHelper.GetData unguarded NPE in ~8 hot paths, per-city-load skill re-inject, BizManBusiness.SetUpTabs/SetTab hard-coded tab list) - that risk is unchanged and applies to BOTH new skills. Grouping "by game product category": INFEASIBLE - no category concept exists. Modeling a department as a "subset of stations/shelves": INFEASIBLE as a stock model - showcase shelves are not assignable and registers are not product-scoped; instance-id shelf tagging is possible but fragile across remodels (opt-in, self-healing only). The restock request->approve loop: does not exist in-game, 100% mod-arbitrated, but needs no Harmony - it is pure mod-domain logic over the existing contract.
openQuestions: Department = pure product-name bucket, or also let the player tag physical ShowcaseShelf ItemInstance ids? Recommend product-name bucket as the core; shelf-id tagging churns on remodel (ids change when items are removed/replaced) so keep it opt-in and self-healing (drop unknown ids on load, fall back to the name list).

A store can have multiple DeliveryContracts (one per wholesaler); the mod currently grabs the FIRST (DeliveryContracts.Get). Merged department requests must be split across the right contracts, or the mod must standardize on one contract per store. Decide the rule.
Team Leader -> Store Manager approval is entirely mod-arbitrated. Need a concrete over-budget trim rule: pro-rata across departments, primary-products-first, or a per-department/TL priority weight.

Wage ladder (~$16 employee -> ~$30 Store Manager): Team Leader needs its own custom SkillData with wage baseline/multiplier feeding EmployeeHelper.CalculateHourlyWageForSkill. Confirm the two new skills' relative wage tiers and that both get the Harmony guard on SkillHelper.GetData.

Does GetAssignableItems() ever return showcase shelves for any specific retail BusinessType (e.g. a deli/butcher counter item flagged assignable)? Worth a per-business check only if the optional spatial shelf-tagging path is pursued.

Should a dormant/absent Team Leader freeze only its department's contract lines (leaving other departments running) or fall back to whole-store planning? The mod's current Dormant handling is per-plan, not per-department.
